Prepare a person-local table for sticky DP releases

Source: R/privacy.R
ds.omop.dp.prepare.Rd

Runs a typed omop_recipe or omop_plan on every server through the community-tool method omopDpPlanExecuteDS (dsOMOP 2.9.1 or later), which builds the tables with the same plan engine as ds.omop.plan.execute and seals them with the authenticated DP provenance that ds.omop.dp.release requires. Ordinary table loading never involves DP; use this function only to define the population and the derived variables of a DP release (for example an age at a public reference year). The analyst chooses that population; the data custodian owns every privacy setting (epsilon, caps, whether DP is available).

Usage

ds.omop.dp.prepare(x, out = NULL, symbol = "omop", conns = NULL)

Arguments

x

An omop_recipe or omop_plan.

out

Output symbols, as in recipe_execute and ds.omop.plan.execute.

symbol

Character; the session symbol used when the OMOP connection was initialised (default "omop").

conns

DSI connection object(s). If NULL (the default), the connections stored in the active session are used.

Value

The named output-to-symbol mapping, invisibly.

Details

Prepared tables keep their concept identifiers as stored (no concept-factor harmonization), and filtering, merging or otherwise manipulating them drops the DP provenance: define the whole release population in the recipe.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
recipe <- omop_recipe(
  variables = omop_variable_age(name = "age_at_2025", year = 2025),
  outputs = omop_output(name = "ages", type = "wide")
)
ds.omop.dp.prepare(recipe, out = c(ages = "DP_ages"))
ds.omop.dp.release("DP_ages", omop_privacy(
  "numeric_histogram", variable = "age_at_2025",
  breaks = seq(0, 120, by = 10), reducer = "mean"))
} # }
